Now I have everything. Here's the full breakdown:

---

## Hono Router Implementations

### RegExpRouter
**File:** `src/router/reg-exp-router/router.ts:122`

The fastest router. On `add()` it accumulates routes and middleware into internal maps. On the **first `match()` call**, it builds a single compiled mega-RegExp for all routes via a trie (`Trie.buildRegExp()`), then discards the raw route data (`#middleware = #routes = undefined`, line 218). Every subsequent match is a single regex exec — O(1) regardless of route count.

**Limitation:** throws `UnsupportedPathError` for paths combining both `:param` and `*` wildcards (the trie can't represent them).

---

### TrieRouter
**File:** `src/router/trie-router/router.ts:5`

Uses an actual trie (prefix tree) via the `Node` class (`src/router/trie-router/node.ts:25`). Inserts routes segment-by-segment on `add()`. Each `match()` traverses the trie. Handles all path shapes including mixed param+wildcard ones, making it the fallback when RegExpRouter fails. Slower per-request than RegExpRouter at scale but works universally.

---

### SmartRouter
**File:** `src/router/smart-router/router.ts:4`

A meta-router — it holds no routes itself, just delegates to a list of real routers. During `add()` it buffers every route (line 18). On the **first `match()`** call it feeds all buffered routes into each candidate router in order, catching `UnsupportedPathError`, and commits to the first one that succeeds (line 46: `this.match = router.match.bind(router)`). After that, it's completely out of the critical path — calls go straight to the winner's `match`.

**Default `Hono` constructor** (`src/hono.ts:30`) uses `SmartRouter([RegExpRouter, TrieRouter])`: tries the faster RegExpRouter first, falls back to TrieRouter for unsupported paths.

---

### LinearRouter
**File:** `src/router/linear-router/router.ts:11`

The simplest possible implementation: a flat `[method, path, handler][]` array. `add()` is a single push. `match()` iterates every route linearly, doing string/regex checks per-route on each request — O(n) per call. Has zero compile-time cost so registration is instant.

**Limitation:** throws `UnsupportedPathError` for paths with both `:param` and `*` (line 137).

**Used in** `src/preset/quick.ts:20` via `SmartRouter([LinearRouter, TrieRouter])` — the "quick" preset prioritizes fast startup over sustained throughput. Good for short-lived runtimes (Cloudflare Workers where the isolate is cold frequently) or apps with very few routes.

---

### PatternRouter
**File:** `src/router/pattern-router/router.ts:8`

Each route is stored as a pre-compiled `RegExp` (one per route, line 34). `match()` iterates routes and calls `pattern.exec(path)` per entry, extracting named groups as params. Supports all path types.

**Used in** `src/preset/tiny.ts:19` directly (no SmartRouter wrapper) — the "tiny" preset. It has the smallest footprint and zero clever machinery, making it ideal for size-constrained environments where bundle size matters more than raw throughput.

---

### Decision tree

| Router | Matching speed | Registration speed | Route support | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegExpRouter | Fastest (single regex) | Slower (compile on first match) | No param+wildcard combos | Default; high-traffic long-lived processes |
| TrieRouter | Fast (trie walk) | Fast | Universal | Fallback for RegExpRouter; used via SmartRouter |
| SmartRouter | Delegates to winner | Buffered | Whatever its sub-routers support | Always — it's the default wrapper |
| LinearRouter | Slow O(n) | Instant | No param+wildcard combos | Short-lived runtimes, tiny route tables (`preset/quick`) |
| PatternRouter | Slow O(n) | Fast | Universal | Smallest bundle, size-constrained (`preset/tiny`) |
